title: Correct public claims and document deferred capability gaps
description:
Update README, CHANGELOG, command documentation, and the audit artifacts to describe only behavior verified in the stabilized extension. Remove or qualify claims of full folder CRUD/move, request-scoped variable editing, workspace mode, cookie-jar support, proxy configuration, and local file bodies unless implementation and tests prove them. Record these substantial items as deferred product-capability work rather than silently expanding stabilization scope.

Document the actual command set and startup behavior; storage location, schema, backup/recovery, and global-versus-workspace scope; variable precedence and unresolved-value behavior; authentication/SecretStorage and redaction guarantees; import/export limits; HTTP limits; and code generation as starter snippets. Provide migration and recovery guidance without exposing internal secrets.

Keep the evidence-backed architecture audit, finding registry, and remediation plan current as work closes. Do not introduce competitive comparisons or Postman-parity promises. Every feature statement must link to a test, implementation, or explicit limitation.

checklist.text: Audit every public feature and command claim against the final implementation and tests
Remove or qualify unsupported folder, request-variable, workspace, cookie, proxy, and local-file capabilities
Document commands, startup behavior, storage scope/schema, migrations, backups, recovery, and limits
Document variable precedence, auth SecretStorage, redaction, import/export behavior, and HTTP limits
Describe generated code as starter snippets and state language/runtime assumptions
Update the architecture audit, finding registry, remediation status, README, and CHANGELOG consistently
Record deferred capability work explicitly without competitive comparisons or unverified parity claims
